newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close up near the day's highs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close up near the day's highs.

text.p: 1440 GMT - Swiss shares extended early gains toward the end of the session to close more than one percent higher.
Derivatives transactions led to high volatility, dealers said. "The pace with which the market changes direction is enourmous," one dealer said.
He said sentiment remained favourable given the prospect of low interest rates. The firming dollar was seen boosting prices.
* Nestle rebounded from a longer weak period to close 17 francs higher at 1,968. Dealers said expectations ahead of half-year sales, due out on Thursday, were high.
* Blue-chip SMI up 82.8 points, or 1.42 percent, to 5,927.5.
The SMI reached the day's high at 5,927.5 points.
* The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 44.91 points, or 1.22 percent, to end at 3,730.31.
Bourse volume reached 2.74 billion Swiss francs.
* Roche profited from Tuesday's first half-year sales figures, which came in at the upper end of market expections, dealers said. Roche certificates soared 385 francs to 14,810.
* Novartis registered shares underperformed the market, advancing 24 francs to 2,441.
* UBS bearers climbed 21 francs to 1,700.
* Sulzer rebounded from recent lows, advancing 17 francs to 1,227. One trader said the share profited from the float of subsidiary Sulzer Medica on Monday.

* Sulzer Medica SMENn.S was up 18.50 francs to 434.5. Sulzer Medica chief executive Andre Buchel told the Swiss business newspaper Finanz und Wirtschaft the company would not wait long before making acquisitions in its core businesses of orthopaedics and cardiovascular equipment.
* Among financials, SBC, Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Re were among the biggest winners.
* SBC was up eight francs at 418. On Tuesday it announced an alliance in the Japanese market with Japanese bank LTCB, including taking stakes in each other and setting up three joint ventures,
Dealers said the deal was favourable for SBC.
* On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), volume was high in UBS options and SMI futures.
UBS accounted for almost half of all 136,233 options traded.
On the futures side, 13,906 SMI futures changed hands. The high volume was mainly due to Friday's expiry of July contracts.
-- Martin Gelnar, Zurich Newsroom, ++41 1 631 7342
